headline: Sandy Hook starter pack.
subhead: Key landmarks, water access, and commuter routes in this Newtown village. Swipe.

slides.title: Upper Paugussett State Forest
slides.text: Offers miles of marked hiking and mountain bike trails along Lake Lillinonah, with unpaved fire roads open year-round.

slides.title: Eichler's Cove marina
slides.text: Town-owned water access on Lake Zoar featuring a public boat launch, marina slips, and a freshwater beach.

slides.title: Sandy Hook Village center
slides.text: A compact commercial district anchored along the Pootatuck River, with sidewalks connecting local businesses and municipal parking.

slides.title: Interstate 84 corridor
slides.text: Highway exits 10 and 11 provide direct highway links west toward Danbury and east toward Waterbury and Hartford.

slides.title: Annual village tree lighting
slides.text: A seasonal December gathering centered around the historic village lampposts and storefronts, hosted every year since 2000.

caption:
Exit 10 off I-84 drops you right into Sandy Hook's core, where the Pootatuck River cuts past the storefronts.

If you are looking at Sandy Hook CT this November, here is the ground-level layout. You have Upper Paugussett State Forest to the north for trail systems and Lake Lillinonah views. South of that sits Lake Zoar and Eichler's Cove, which gives Newtown residents direct boat slips and shoreline access.

Commuters use exits 10 and 11 to reach Danbury or Hartford without cutting across town. The village center stays active through winter, leading into the annual December tree lighting by the river.
